transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Hayes (CISO, ClearHealth), Leah Ortiz (Identity Engineer), Daniel Park (Lead DevOps)

--- Optional auto sections present ---
Topics: SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/encryption, data residency
Questions: SSO integration steps, SCIM group syncing cadence, RBAC granularity, audit log retention and export

Transcript:
00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. We're here to walk through SSO and provisioning and make sure it fits your security posture.
00:12 Marcus: Thanks Alex. Quick note, I'm Marcus, CISO. We need to ensure least-privilege and that audit logs meet our compliance team needs, SOC2 specifically.
00:22 Priya: Absolutely, Marcus. We'll cover SAML, SCIM, RBAC mapping, and the audit/export story. Quick question  do you guys have Okta as your IdP today?
00:30 Leah: Yes, Okta for most teams, we also have a few Azure AD tenants for partners. We want group-based provisioning and SCIM so we can auto-on/off-board.
00:40 Alex: Great. Outline: SAML for auth, SCIM for user/group provisioning, RBAC role model mapping to groups, session and token lifetimes, audit logs to S3 or API, and KMS for key management.
01:02 Daniel: From infra side, we'll need details on where audit logs land and whether we can ingest into our SIEM. Also, whatever staging access you need for testing.
01:15 Priya: We support SAML 2.0 SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. For SCIM we speak SCIM 2.0 standard endpoints. Common gotcha: group attribute names - Okta uses 'members', some IDPs call it 'memberships' or 'skim' in older tools, so mapping is needed.
01:36 Leah: "skim"? you mean SCIM but I've seen the scanner mis-take, ok yes. We map groups in Okta to access levels. How fine-grained can Redwood RBAC be?
01:48 Priya: We provide built-in roles: admin, engineer, viewer, plus you can create custom roles with per-route and per-model permissions. You can map SCIM groups to roles. We recommend least-privilege: create role clusters per environment (prod, staging) and limit model management to a small admin group.
02:05 Marcus: For healthcare we need separation  only a handful of engineers can update model rollouts. Can roles restrict by model and by route?
02:14 Priya: Yes, roles can be scoped to models and API routes. Example: role 'model-deployer' with ability to perform rollouts on pinned models, but not change billing or stats export. We'll share a role matrix.
02:25 Alex: On SAML specifics, we'll send a SAML SP metadata file, certs, ACS URL, entity ID. We support signed assertions and encrypted attributes. Do you require attribute encryption or just signing?
02:38 Marcus: We'd like assertions signed at minimum. For PHI-sensitive flows maybe encrypted attributes, but for our use case signing is acceptable. We will confirm with compliance.
02:46 Priya: Cool. For SCIM, provisioning events are create, update, deactivate. We support group sync at configurable polling intervals or near-real-time via push. For Okta we usually recommend initial full sync, then incremental.
03:02 Leah: Incremental is preferred. How do you handle group membership conflicts when a user is in multiple groups mapped to different roles?
03:12 Priya: We have precedence rules; the most-privileged role wins by default, but you can override to deny escalation. We also support attribute-based role resolution if you want to use custom SCIM attributes.
03:28 Daniel: About audit logs  retention and export. We need logs for 2 years, and ability to stream to our S3 or to pull via API into Splunk.
03:38 Alex: Redwood offers audit logs with configurable retention; standard plan stores 90 days, enterprise can extend to multi-year. Logs can be exported to customer S3 buckets or sent via secure syslog or API. We can provision an S3 bucket with a write-only role for us to deliver logs.
03:55 Marcus: Encryption at rest and in transit? KMS integration?
04:00 Priya: At rest we use AES-256 and our platform supports bringing-your-own-key (BYOK) via AWS KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments. For hosted we offer customer-managed keys for encryption of secrets and data-at-rest. In transit is TLS 1.2/1.3.
04:17 Leah: For private deployment (on-prem) we assume keys remain on-prem. For the hosted Redwood, can we rotate keys regularly and have audit of key use?
04:26 Alex: Yes, key rotation flows are supported and we log KMS operations; audit trail includes key usage. For enterprise customers we support HSM-backed keys and provide key rotation docs.
04:40 Marcus: Data residency  we process inference in specific regions, can we guarantee data doesn't leave region?
04:47 Priya: We support region pinning per deployment: you can pin to us-east-1 or eu-west-1 etc. For private Dedicated or Private deployments, data never leaves your VPC or on-prem cluster. We'll note region in the SLA.
05:02 Leah: On SCIM attribute mapping, do you support custom attributes like 'employeeType' or 'department'? We want to use department for default routing.
05:12 Priya: Yes, custom attributes are supported. We'll include an attribute mapping example: okta->urn:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:department.
05:24 Alex: Quick pause  transcription note: sometimes SCIM gets transcribed as 'skim' or 'scan' in older exports, it doesn't affect config but FYI for docs.
05:35 Marcus: Ha, noted. Back to RBAC, do you log role assumption and admin actions? We need immutable logs for who initiated a model rollback or rollout.
05:45 Priya: Yes, admin actions are recorded with actor, timestamp, IP, and request context. We also provide request-level tracing to see token-level cost and latency for audits.
06:00 Daniel: For SSO sessions, can we enforce session length and idle time? And do you support MFA enforcement via our IdP?
06:10 Priya: Session lifetime is configurable; we support short-lived sessions and token refresh. MFA is enforced by your IdP, so yes  Redwood honors the auth result from the IdP including MFA.
06:22 Marcus: Compliance  you mentioned SOC 2. Do you publish a report and can we get an auditor's letter?
06:28 Alex: We are SOC 2 Type II compliant and can share the report under NDA. We also maintain ISO certs; we can arrange a security package for your procurement team.
06:37 Leah: On provisioning pace, if a SCIM sync fails due to rate limits, do you queue and retry?
06:44 Priya: Yes, we have exponential backoff and a retry queue for provisioning operations. We'll surface errors to the audit logs and to the SCIM admin dashboard.
06:55 Daniel: About least-privilege: if a developer needs temporary elevated rights for debugging, is there a time-bound elevation flow?
07:05 Priya: We don't currently offer a built-in ephemeral elevation UI, but we support short-lived role tokens and you can programmatically grant a role with an expiry. We can help set up a workflow with your governance tooling.
07:18 Marcus: That works, but we want guardrails to prevent accidental permanent grants.
07:24 Alex: We'll include RBAC templates with recommended guardrails.
07:30 Priya: One more technical detail  our SCIM supports bulk PATCH operations for group membership so initial syncs are faster; incremental uses delta tokens. For SCIM we expect Okta to send userName, id, displayName, emails and can accept custom attrs.
07:52 Leah: For testing, we'd like to do a pilot with 10-30 users and one group mapped to 'reader' and another to 'engineer'.
07:59 Alex: Sounds good. We'll set up a staging SP, send metadata. Priya will provision a testing tenant.
08:06 Priya: Action items recap coming. Any other questions from procurement side?
08:12 Marcus: Pricing aside, final ask: we need a clear audit export format and proof of encryption and key handling for procurement.
08:20 Alex: We'll attach the security kit: SOC2 report (NDA), encryption/KMS whitepaper, SAML/SCIM integration guide, and RBAC mapping template.
08:28 Daniel: Great. Also want to confirm logging format  JSON-lines with scheme?
08:33 Priya: Yes, audit logs are JSON-lines with fields: timestamp, actor, action, resource, result, request_id. We'll include the schema in the docs.
08:45 Leah: One small nit  SCIM group membership resolution: if we remove a user from Okta, do you soft-delete or deactivate?
08:52 Priya: We deactivate by default and keep a tombstone for 30 days configurable, enterprise can extend.
09:00 Marcus: Ok that aligns with our retention rules.
09:05 Alex: Recap and next steps  send metadata and docs, share RBAC matrix, customer to provide IdP metadata, schedule pilot.
09:15 Marcus: Thanks, appreciate the detail.
09:18 Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up by email with docs and action items.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heard terms (e.g., 'skim' for SCIM). This artifact intended for internal integration work and procurement review.
